rule_sets.py:636-643 builds Not(Paren(Is(col, NULL))) with the comment in question. MySQL 8.0 docs (Operator Precedence / HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE): by default NOT ranks below comparison operators including IS, so NOT x IS NULL is NOT (x IS NULL). With HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE, NOT binds tighter than comparison operators, so NOT x IS NULL is (NOT x) IS NULL. The docs' example is NOT a BETWEEN b AND c becoming (NOT a) BETWEEN b AND c, and IS is at the same comparison level. The comment matches this. I did not run MySQL, so this rests on the documented precedence only. The code also parenthesizes, so it is correct under both modes.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:636-643: IsNotNullRule compiles to exp.Not(this=exp.Paren(this=exp.Is(col, NULL))), i.e. `NOT (x IS NULL)`. The parentheses force the IS NULL to bind first, so HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE (which only changes how a bare NOT binds to its operand, making `NOT x IS NULL` read as `(NOT x) IS NULL`) cannot alter it. Inside any_of/all_of (lines 644-647) the node is an atomic NOT(...) unit combined via exp.or_/exp.and_; under HIGH_NOT, NOT already binds tighter than AND/OR, so `NOT (x IS NULL) AND y` still groups as (NOT (x IS NULL)) AND y. The doc line (docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md:42) matches this. The code comment at 637-638 agrees. The factory also removes HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE anyway (factory.py:67), so the claim holds independently.
